documents.title: University of Wyoming syllabus template with sample AI language
documents.stance_why: The template only "recommend[s] that faculty include a section focused on permitted/unpermitted AI technology use" and offers four sample options (prohibited, prior permission, acknowledgement, freely permitted). It sets no single university rule and leaves the choice to instructors, so the stance is delegates with tiers.
tiers: Option 2: Use only with prior permission
Option 4: Use is freely permitted with no acknowledgement
documents.summary: A university syllabus template from Academic Affairs that recommends every syllabus carry an AI section near the academic dishonesty statement. It supplies four sample statements, adapted from the University of Delaware, ranging from prohibition to free use, and leaves the choice to each instructor.

units.why: The template says "We recommend that faculty include a section focused on permitted/unpermitted AI technology use in each of their syllabi", a recommendation to instructors to state AI expectations in every syllabus, which is exactly P09 (a recommendation, hence should, not must).
units.anchor: include a section focused on permitted/unpermitted AI technology use in each of their syllabi

units.why: The same passage places the AI section "generally in the location of their Student Academic Dishonesty statement", a placement suggestion for communicating expectations; it is part of the syllabus-statement practice so P09 with a fit note.
units.anchor: generally in the location of their Student Academic Dishonesty statement
units.fit_note: Adds where in the syllabus the AI section goes (next to the academic dishonesty statement), which the type does not name.

units.why: "it is important that faculty clearly communicate their expectations of course collaboration policies (with other students)" asks instructors to communicate collaboration rules alongside AI rules; no type covers collaboration-policy communication, so the nearest is P09.
units.anchor: clearly communicate their expectations of course collaboration policies (with other students)
units.fit_note: Concerns communicating collaboration-with-peers expectations, not only AI expectations.

units.why: "We offer the following language as draft material ... that instructors may want to consider" is the university supplying sample syllabus language for instructors to adopt, matching P110 (templates), with the optional "may want to consider" wording.
units.anchor: We offer the following language as draft material (adapted from University of Delaware)

units.why: The four headed options (prohibited, prior permission, acknowledgement, freely permitted) are named categories of AI use that instructors choose from; this is P05 (named tiers) and also leaves the choice to instructors, but the tier structure is the more specific fit than P04.
units.anchor: Option 2: Use only with prior permission
units.frag_end: no special documentation or citation is required.
units.fit_note: The four options are sample statements an instructor may pick, so the choice is also left to the instructor (P04).

units.why: Option 1 says "Students are not permitted to use advanced automated artificial intelligence or machine learning tools on assignments", a ban on AI for assignments in the sample statement, so P01 with must-not and prohibit.
units.anchor: Students are not permitted to use advanced automated artificial intelligence or machine learning tools

units.why: "Each student is expected to complete each assignment without substantive assistance from others, including automated tools" asks that submitted work be the student's own without AI help; closest is P19 (do not have AI produce the work), and it also treats automated tools like other people.
units.anchor: complete each assignment without substantive assistance from others, including automated tools
units.fit_note: Phrased as expectation of unassisted work, covering assistance from people and automated tools alike.

units.why: Option 2 says AI tools are permitted "if instructor permission is obtained in advance", which is AI allowed only after explicit prior approval, i.e. P107.
units.anchor: if instructor permission is obtained in advance

units.why: "Unless given permission to use those tools, each student is expected to complete each assignment without substantive assistance" states what applies when no permission is given, the default prohibition, which is P06 (fallback) within the option.
units.anchor: Unless given permission to use those tools, each student is expected to complete each assignment
units.policy: Unless given permission to use those tools, each student is expected to complete each assignment without substantive assistance from others, including automated tools.

units.why: Option 3 says AI use is permitted "if that use is properly documented and credited", so use is allowed with mandatory acknowledgement; P24 (disclose with each submission) fits, since the condition is disclosure.
units.anchor: if that use is properly documented and credited

units.why: The example citation "Chat-GPT-3. (YYYY, Month DD of query). 'Text of your query.' Generated using OpenAI." requires the tool, date, query and URL, and "Material generated using other tools should follow a similar citation convention", which is P25 (cite tool, prompt, output).
units.anchor: Material generated using other tools should follow a similar citation convention.
units.frag_start: text generated using ChatGPT-3 should include

units.why: Option 4 says "Students are permitted to use advanced automated artificial intelligence or machine learning tools on assignments in this course; no special documentation or citation is required", an open permission with no disclosure, so P02.
units.anchor: no special documentation or citation is required
units.fit_note: Also states that no disclosure is needed (the opposite of P24).

notes: Only one included document; AI content is a single section of a syllabus template. Sample options are templates, so unit-level modalities describe the sample wording.
